answer_raw:
MLX is faster for pure performance benchmarks, but Ollama is the better choice for agent-based workflows.

The choice between them isn't symmetric; if you are running autonomous agents (like Claude Code), you should use **Ollama** to serve the model, whereas **MLX** is better suited for overnight benchmarks or high-throughput testing [1]. On an M4 Max, MLX can run a 35B model at roughly twice the speed of Ollama (60-70+ tok/s vs ~35 tok/s) [7]. However, for your 48GB M4 Pro, the decision depends on the use case: use **Ollama** for developer-friendly agent deployment and **MLX** for maximum single-request throughput [1][3].

Regarding your capacity, you can realistically run **70B models** using Q4 quantization [6]. With 48GB of unified memory, your hardware can handle 30B models at full precision or 70B models with 4-bit quantization [6]. On an M4 Pro, the GPU memory limit is typically around 40GB of the 48GB available [2].
